requirements_summary.summary: Participium is a web application for the Municipality of Turin enabling citizens to report urban issues (e.g., potholes, trash) via an interactive map or Telegram bot. Reports undergo a lifecycle: Pending Approval -> Assigned (to technical offices) -> In Progress -> Resolved/Rejected/Suspended. The system supports external maintainers (with or without platform access), internal communication channels, notifications (email/push), and detailed statistics for administrators.

requirements.text:
As a technical office staff member/external maintainer
I want to exchange information and comments on the report internally
So that coordination happens without exposing internal notes to citizens
expected_behaviors: coordination happens without exposing internal notes to citizens

requirements.text:
As a citizen
I want to register with my name and username 
So that I can access the Participium system and submit reports.
constraints: Registration is required before submitting reports.
expected_behaviors: I can access the Participium system and submit reports

requirements.text:
As a citizen
I want to create a new report through a Telegram bot
So that I can quickly notify the public administration about an issue in my area.
constraints:
Allows the citizen to open a new report by selecting a location on the Turin map, entering a title, description, choosing a category, and attaching up to three photos. The bot also asks if the report should be anonymous.

Example command:

/newreport → Starts the guided process to create a new issue report with location, title, description, category, photos, and anonymity preference.
expected_behaviors: I can quickly notify the public administration about an issue in my area

requirements.text:
As a citizen 
I want to check my report status through a Telegram bot 
So that I can quickly get updates.
constraints:
Check the status of their own reports, receiving an updated list with any changes.
Example commands:

/myreports → Lists all your submitted reports with their current status.

/reportstatus 12345 → Shows details and current status of report ID 12345.

domain_rules: Reports must be in 'Pending Approval' state until the Organization Office performs preliminary verification.
Accepted reports move to 'Assigned' state and are sent to the competent technical office depending on the problem category.
Rejected reports require an explanation from the Municipality Organization Office.
Once approved, accepted reports immediately become visible on the Participium portal (map and table).
Unregistered users can view reports on maps but cannot submit new reports.
Once a report has been inserted, it cannot be modified or deleted by the citizen.
An anonymous user's name is still visible to staff and only hidden in the Turin map of reports for citizens.
Only technical office staff members can have multiple roles.
The roles 'municipal public relations officer' and 'municipal administrator' are automatically associated with the Organization Office.
Email is a mandatory field for registration and can also be used for login.
External maintainers are added by the system administrator.
Each maintainer should have their own individual account.
Assignment logic is left to the teams, as done for municipality technical offices.
Comments/information exchanged between a technical office and an external maintainer are report-specific and reserved (not visible to citizens).
Communication between a technical office and external maintainers without access to Participium is out of scope.
Notifications/messages can be set to either be sent in real time or when the page is refreshed, depending on user preference.
edge_cases: If a report is rejected, it must include an explanation from the Municipality Organization Office.
If a citizen chooses anonymity, their name is hidden in public views but visible to staff.
When zooming out on the map, reports can be grouped into a cumulative report showing total numbers.
When downloading the summary table, if filters are active, only filtered data is included in the CSV.
External maintainers without platform access (Case 2) update the technical office out of Participium; the technical office staff member moves the report to 'Resolved' manually.
Automatic assignment of issues of a certain category is possible only if previously set by the municipal administrator.
assumptions: The system uses OpenStreetMap as the standard layer for geolocation.
The Municipality of Turin's organizational structure (technical offices) follows the official chart provided in the description.
Telegram bot integration requires the user to have configured a Telegram username in their profile.
Email notifications are sent by default unless explicitly disabled in the configuration panel.
The 'Organization Office' acts as the initial reviewer for all reports before assignment.

authentication_notes: NextAuth endpoints at /api/auth/{nextauth} handle session management and login callbacks but do not enforce auth_required in the schema.
Telegram report creation (/api/telegram/reports POST) returns 401, suggesting authentication may be enforced at runtime despite auth_required being null.
dependencies: User must register Telegram account via /api/telegram/registration before using /api/telegram/isAuthenticated or fetching reports.
Report creation (/api/telegram/reports POST) likely depends on prior user registration and potentially authentication (indicated by 401 response).
POST /api/telegram/registration -> GET /api/telegram/reports/{id}: User must be registered to access their reports.
POST /api/auth/{nextauth} -> POST /api/telegram/reports: Report creation returns 401, implying prior authentication is required.

risks: auth_required field is null for all operations, but some (e.g., report creation) return 401, creating ambiguity about when auth is actually enforced.
NextAuth endpoints are catch-all routes; specific behavior depends on the path segment (e.g., session vs callback), which is not explicitly detailed beyond generic descriptions.
